- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of sentiment decay.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving >2% from 30-day moving average, model tends to overreact; apply a “reversion dampener” to bring forecast closer to 30-day MA.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–2 days in response to sentiment shifts; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change to avoid delay.
